title: Grateful Dead Live at Baltimore Civic Center on 1982-04-19
lineage: SHNs were decoded to wave and Audition 3.0 was used to reassemble the tracks back to 1 long wave.  Audition 3.0 was used to align & synch the SBD & AUD sources.  Audition 3.0 used to adjust the volume for AUDs, matrix/CTR and LFE channels.
source: Matrix 2 Source Mix - SBD (shn id 89313) MAC > R1 7.5ips 1/4 track > Technics RS-1506 > Grace designs Lunatec V3 (pre only) > Korg MR-1000 > DSD-DFF 1bit 5.64 Mhz > Audio Gate SW > 24/96 WAV + AUD (shn id 19420) MAC (Taped by Steven Martin, modified Nakamichi CM-700 mics > Sony TC-D5M) > Nak Dragon playback > Cardas audiophile cables > HHB CDR 800 master CD

ai_review.summary: Matrix mix (60 % SBD/40 % AUD) sounds excellent and captures a killer 4‑6‑82 Baltimore show with standout second‑set gems like The Wheel → Truckin' → Good Lovin' and an emotional Brokedown Palace.
ai_review.review: The Tobin matrix blend delivers crystal‑clear instrument separation that many reviewers call the best sounding source for this concert, while the performance itself is hailed as one of ’82’s finest – especially the second set’s seamless flow and powerhouse versions of The Wheel, Truckin', Good Lovin' and a soaring Peggy‑O.  A few listeners note occasional drop‑outs on Terrapin Station and minor roughness on Franklin's Tower, but overall the show is described as killer and emotionally resonant.

ai_rating.rationale: Over half of the reviews are 5‑star praises focusing on both superb matrix sound quality and an outstanding performance; only a few minor criticisms keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: 60 % soundboard, 40 % audience mix praised for sweet balance and clarity; one reviewer notes occasional cut‑outs on Terrapin Station but overall the mix is described as the best‑sounding source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set is highlighted as a near‑perfect arc with tight transitions from Feel Like A Stranger through Franklin's Tower, Estimated Prophet, Terrapin Station, Drums into an inspired Raven Space and a string of classics that many fans rank among the best ever.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Immaculate vocals, exquisite phrasing and a long, soaring solo on Peggy‑O; generally described as 'killer' throughout the night.
band_member_comments.Phil: Emotional presence at the end – held out his arms during Brokedown Palace and lingered onstage, showing deep connection with the audience.
